method: Every result is a closed-form transmission-line estimate worked in millimetres. The frequency is entered in GHz and the substrate thickness in millimetres or mils (1 mil = 0.0254 mm); frequency must lie from 0.1 to 50 GHz, relative permittivity from 1.1 to 20 and thickness from 0.05 to 10 mm or 2 to 400 mil. The free-space wavelength is 299.792458 / f millimetres. Patch width is half that wavelength times sqrt(2/(er+1)), the usual TM10 choice that places the radiating edges about a half wave apart in the dielectric. The width-to-thickness ratio r = W/h feeds the effective permittivity ee = (er+1)/2 + (er-1)/2 / sqrt(1+12/r). Fringing fields extend each radiating edge by delta L = 0.412 h (ee+0.3)(r+0.264) / ((ee-0.258)(r+0.8)), and the physical resonant length is L = lambda0/(2 sqrt(ee)) - 2 delta L. Reported values round half up: millimetre lengths and wavelengths to two places, mils to whole mils, the fringing extension to three places, effective permittivity to four, the width-to-thickness ratio to four and the thickness-to-wavelength ratio to five. The guided wavelength is lambda0/sqrt(ee). A suggested ground plane adds a 6h margin on every side, giving W+12h by L+12h. Inputs that leave no positive resonant length are refused with a message, and the page warns when the width-to-thickness ratio falls below 1, when h/lambda0 exceeds 0.05 (an electrically thick substrate) or above 20 GHz. The model ignores feed inset, copper thickness, substrate loss, surface waves and mutual coupling, so the resonance must be confirmed by simulation and measurement. Everything runs locally in the browser with no storage, uploads or network requests.
